_note: Films and series for /cultura/filmes-e-series: title, year, maker and our own short description, nothing else. No streaming links (they change). `level` is our estimate of how much Portuguese you need to enjoy it with Portuguese subtitles. Each text says whether you hear European or Brazilian (or African) Portuguese. Years and directors are from memory of well-documented works and are listed 'to verify' in the culture report. Rewritten for the Portuguese course 2026-11-21 (culture run); the group ids `espana` and `america` are kept for the i18n keys.

items.title: A Canção de Lisboa
items.text: A medical student in Lisbon spends more time in the fado houses than at his books, and his aunts from the country are coming to visit. An early sound comedy in European Portuguese; the old recording takes some getting used to.

items.title: O Pátio das Cantigas
items.text: Neighbours around one Lisbon courtyard argue, flirt and sing during the festas of June. A classic comedy that many Portuguese people can still quote.

items.title: Aniki-Bóbó
items.text: Children in the streets and on the riverbank of Porto, a small theft and a first love. Short, simple dialogue and many pictures of old Porto.

items.title: Capitães de Abril
items.text: The night and day of 25 April 1974, told through the young officers who ended the dictatorship. A good way to learn the history and the words around it.

items.title: Aquele Querido Mês de Agosto
items.text: Summer in the mountain villages of central Portugal: village festas, bands, emigrants home for August. Half documentary, half story, and slow.

items.title: Tabu
items.text: An old woman in Lisbon today, then her youth in colonial Africa told by a narrator. In black and white; the second half has almost no dialogue.

items.title: Sangue do Meu Sangue
items.text: A family in a housing estate on the edge of Lisbon, and the secrets that hold it together. Fast, overlapping everyday speech, a real test for your listening.

items.title: Variações
items.text: The life of António Variações, a barber from the Minho who became a pop singer in Lisbon in the early 1980s. Lots of music and clear dialogue.

items.title: Glória
items.text: A spy story in a small Ribatejo village in the 1960s, around a real radio station that broadcast to the East. Shows the Estado Novo years; some lines are in English and Russian.

items.title: Conta-me Como Foi
items.text: One Lisbon family from the late 1960s into the years after the revolution, seen by the youngest son. Everyday European Portuguese and a lot of recent history.

groups.title: From Brazil and the other Portuguese-speaking countries

items.title: Central do Brasil
items.text: Brazil: a former teacher who writes letters for people who cannot write travels north with a boy who has lost his mother. Brazilian Portuguese, clear and not too fast.

items.title: O Auto da Compadecida
items.text: Brazil: two poor, clever friends in the backlands of the North-East trick everyone, right up to the Last Judgement. Very funny, with a strong regional accent.

items.title: Cidade de Deus
items.text: Brazil: a boy grows up in a Rio de Janeiro favela between the 1960s and the 1980s and wants to become a photographer. Very violent; fast street slang of Rio.

items.title: Que Horas Ela Volta?
items.text: Brazil: a live-in housekeeper in São Paulo and her daughter, who arrives and does not accept the old rules of the house. Calm everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

items.title: Ainda Estou Aqui
items.text: Brazil, 1971: during the military dictatorship a mother in Rio has to hold her family together after her husband is taken away. Based on a true story; Brazilian Portuguese.

items.title: Terra Sonâmbula
items.text: Mozambique during the civil war: an old man and a boy find a notebook full of stories on a burnt-out bus. Based on the novel by Mia Couto; Mozambican Portuguese.

items.title: Na Cidade Vazia
items.text: Angola, 1991: a boy who has lost his family runs away into Luanda and meets the people of the city. Angolan Portuguese, quiet and serious.
